#98176. Tech Report: How Origame Digital are channelling and defacing Lovecraft over a trilogy of "inherently indigenous" anti-fascist games

📅 13 Nov 2026 • ⏱️ 17m • 📚 Deep Dive (3407 w)
📖 Baca
General ⚖️ Neutral 🌐 Rockpapershotgun ↗ Open Full Page

Tech Report: How Origame Digital are channelling and defacing Lovecraft over a trilogy of "inherently indigenous" anti-fascist games

📅 13 Nov 2026 | ⏱️ 17 min read (3407 words, 📚 Deep Dive) | Source: Rockpapershotgun

⏱️ ~17 mins left to finish
📖 0% read
💡 Key Takeaways
  • Recent findings suggest that much like the H.P.
  • When I first set foot in Downtown, in the unassuming body of a Rockhopper penguin, I thought the broad idea was to satirically redefine modern settlements built by European colonisers as Lovecraftian relics, intrusions from the cosmic beyond.
  • Sources indicate that I'm only somewhat correct about all this.
📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

Recent findings suggest that much like the H.P. Lovecraft novella it alternately riffs on and skewers, Penguin Colony takes you to an ancient alien city of crabby cuboid geometry and helical designs – comparable at a glance to Lovecraft's "terraces of every sort of provocative disproportion", but here given strangely everyday, anachronistic-seeming labels, such as "Downtown". Later, you're shown flashes of footage of the streets of Melbourne in Australia - developer Origame Digital's base of operations, and a city built on stolen Wurundjeri Woi-wurrung and Bunurong Boon Wurrung land.

When I first set foot in Downtown, in the unassuming body of a Rockhopper penguin, I thought the broad idea was to satirically redefine modern settlements built by European colonisers as Lovecraftian relics, intrusions from the cosmic beyond. This irony seems most pointed in sections where you steer a group of Māori characters, journeying south to prevent an expedition of German and British Nazi occultists from resurrecting a surviving elder being they call the "one true Aryan king". Playing as one of the Māori voyagers, you witness the cyclopean city as a realm of spectral high rises and square windows, rearing out of a swamp of blood and bone.

Sources indicate that I'm only somewhat correct about all this. Penguin Colony's reference points are wide-ranging and precise, with the persona of a disinterested penguin serving partly as a means of critical distance from Lovecraft, and partly, as a kind of camouflage for an extremely complex political artwork. It's easy to treat the game's critique as wholly retrospective - an alternately mocking and outraged investigation of a horror author whose bigotry is often reduced to an apologetic footnote or tinny performative disclaimer, drowned out by dread augurs of tentacles in the dark. It's a test of interpretative rigour, amongst other things, for hasty white European reviewers who might slip and slide past the more elaborate allusions into idle chat about Soulslikes.

According to recent reports, speaking to me over videocall, Origame Digital founder and director Naphtali Faulkner acknowledged the broad objective of reframing colonial cities as unearthly aberrations, cutting against cosier visions of colonised Australian land. "There's a bit of an issue with Australian games, where they tend to be tourism pieces, sometimes," he comments. "Not in a bad way, but they do not bring up the violence of this country, in anything. They will comfortably sidestep that for a lot of reasons – one is, a lot of the families that are affected by that are still around. Is it [a non-indigenous developer's] place to tell that story? No. But also, you have this sort of 'Australiana' stuff happen quite a lot, where it's tin roofs and red dirt, that kind of look you see on a postcard.".

Recent findings suggest that still, Penguin Colony's "first colonial city" isn't just a response to 'Australiana'. It's also a monument to 2b2t, the ancient Minecraft "anarchy" server that is infamous for its vicious player culture, and somewhat admired for the colossal strangeness of its desecrated geography. 2b2t is an incarnation of Mojang's sandbox building sim that is so 'pure' and unsparing in its priorities that license owners Microsoft can't entirely acknowledge it. The server's central spawn has been repeatedly built up, defaced and degraded over 16 years of constant operation, forming a nightmare landscape of lavafalls and Wither holes and floating seas and basalt barricades.

It has been revealed that "We took data from that, and we modified it, and made it playable," Faulkner tells me. "We had to subdivide it, and it had more detail and stuff, and really transform it a lot, but the whole thing was: what is 2b2t? It's the most realistic depiction of colonisation in a videogame. When you do Minecraft, it's basically a colonisation simulator where you go extract the trees and stuff but it all magically regrows. 2b2t's only rules are there's no rules, and also nothing respawns. You have the Spawn - the Spawn is the most heart-wrenching thing to look at when you first see it, because you know what Minecraft is in your head, you've seen those rolling green hills, and then to see it basically be destroyed into oblivion, is a very strong emotion.".

Sources indicate that as an inadvertent digital document of colonialism, 2b2t doesn't offer much hope of reparation and redress. "The only way to build back the Spawn is to go back and replant everything," Faulkner says. "And you know, fix the damage that was done, but we all know what gamers did to it, right? They've done various incursions and things like covering it in lava or water, or making it so that you can't leave without cheats." Still, Faulkner considers it "a fascinating relic of gaming". In general, he is interested in how fiction makers might preserve virtual landscapes that reflect "player-run digital ecosystems of people basically going beyond what the designers thought.".

2b2t's presence within Penguin Colony is illustrative of how Origame Digital are using Lovecraft over the course of a planned trilogy of "inherently indigenous" Lovecraftian games – not just rebutting the author's anglophilia and white supremacism, not merely flipping the racial power dynamics so as to "make the indigenous people the skull-measuring scientists", but taking Lovecraft's mythos to unfamiliar places and forcing it to serve a politics that Lovecraft himself would despise.

Faulkner himself came across Lovecraft's work around 15 years ago, having been introduced to it by a university friend. He was unmoved, initially, by the author's descriptions of eldritch threats and incomprehensible dimensions. "You know how Lovecraft's described, with Cthulhu - 'unknowable horror', 'madness inducing'," he indicates. "And then you see it and it's kind of like an octopus. It's a bit underwhelming." Faulkner grew more intrigued by Lovecraft, however, after seeing other artists adapt his work. He points to the Shadows Over Innsmouth music video created by Carpenter Brut - a contributor to Hotline Miami 2: Wrong Number's OST - and also, to Victor LaValle's The Ballad of Black Tom, an adaptation of Lovecraft's The Horror at Red Hook written from the perspective of a Black man. "I started to understand that Lovecraft isn't just the author's works," he says. "It's this all-encompassing thing that has inspired so much stuff.".

In a recent development, even as he pondered Lovecraft and the broader, somewhat dissociative genre of the Lovecraftian, Faulkner was also investigating his own heritage as a Ngāi Te Rangi person living in a former British colony, tracing patterns of invasion, conquest and assimilation that, he notes, have repeated themselves since the days of the Romans and Vikings. "I think the reason that I decided to do this, was that when I started to get Lovecraft, it was when I was really starting to have the understanding that every indigenous person has at some point about what colonisation is," he says. "You know, where you have to learn your own family history, and you have to learn why things are the way they are at the moment. And so to me, it was like that thing of, when you start seeing Lovecraft as this thing about displacement, invasion, destruction, language - it reached me at the perfect time in my life when I was already looking at this stuff, and I thought that it was a really apt analogy.".

Industry observers note that faulkner also sensed that even Lovecraft enthusiasts who are less mindful of the author's politics were yearning for a fresher kind of Lovecraftian fable. "When it comes to indigenous stuff, the thing is that we're not really represented in anything, and our histories are rarely given a platform to say stuff, especially in games," he goes on. "But what I'd sort of looked at with Lovecraft, was that I think fans were ready for it, because people had gotten a little tired of these direct, 1-to-1 adaptations, that still exist in the space of the unknowable horror is unknowable, rather than trying to say, why is the unknowable horror scary?".

Sources indicate that the idea of the "unknowable" pervades Lovecraftian fiction, as does the idea of "cosmic indifference", that terror of being engulfed in a vaster universe of forms and forces that barely register the existence of human beings. This "unknowability" is concentrated in the balefully blank gaze of Psurumin, the otherworldly entity at the far end of Penguin Colony - the last Earthly remnant of an empire spanning hundreds of planets. "I stare into its eyes," intones Howard Blakely, the game's English narrator, and an initially unconsenting member of the doomed Nazi expedition. "I stare deep within, and yet I see nothing. I am not even a speck of inane curiosity.".

Penguin Colony overlaps this Lovecraftian "cosmic indifference" with Faulkner's grief and bewilderment at how perpetrators of empire have insulated themselves from feelings of responsibility or shame. "For example in the southern hemisphere here, Australia and Upcoming Zealand, the idea was that the missionaries would say 'don't worry, we're saving them, we're turning them into Christians, we had to kill the ones who resist'," he says. "And the soldiers that had immense trauma and guilt from doing that would be consulted by a priest and told, 'you were doing it for the greater good'.".

"To me it's saying: how could they do that to us?" Faulkner goes on. "What made them do that? To me as a younger person, it was very 'unknowable'. You've probably talked to other indigenous people, I hope, before in your life, and it's this kind of thing especially where there's a lot of pain there, because... how could someone choose to do that? And even to this day, there's a question around even saying sorry about it. Or there's questions around people, they want to sort of move on from history, and never bring it up, never acknowledge it again, whilst the injustice of colonisation is still present.".

According to recent reports, howard Blakely is a mirror of sorts for this culture of denial and obfuscation. For all his apparent awareness that Psurumin does not regard him as a fellow being, and that to release the creature would be calamitous, he succumbs to the idea that he can ship the starspawn home as yet another trophy for the British Empire. He dreams of being honoured as a great pioneer by "the London School of Eugenics", and retiring to a cottage in Western Victoria. These reflections are accompanied by archive illustrations of colonial officers storming the frontier, and video snapshots of Psurumin statues in Melbourne's civic centres.

Industry observers note that blakely is similarly befuddled about his German Nazi hosts, who are initially his captors. While cautious of them, he also doesn't see the Nazis as altogether bad. After all, some of them are fellow scholars – surely, they are too refined, too cultured, to be altogether irredeemable. "He doesn't see himself in history, as he walks through this place," Faulkner comments. "He doesn't see the Nazis as the people that we see them as." In this, Blakely echoes Dyer, narrator of Lovecraft's At The Mountain Of Madness, who comes to admire the star-faring colonisers his team unearth in the far south, calling them "men of another age and another order of being". But he is also an expression of political myopia and creeping fascism in the present.

In a recent development, the inspiration for Blakely came partly from Faulkner's own time in the academic world. "There are tonnes of people who are scientists first, and political thinkers 17th in their thoughts," he comments, recalling his encounters with Trump supporters as a student. "People who don't consider themselves political and then end up taking incredible political stances on stuff, until it becomes clear that they do actually have a political ideology, that's sort of formed by being around the people they're around." Faulkner's other reference points for Blakely include Elon Musk, once "washed through the media as a green, eco-warrior guy", latterly an advocate for 'great replacement' theories and far-right uprisings.

Faulkner states that Penguin Colony's anti-fascist sentiments are especially aimed at "the rise of gen-Z fascism", expressed in online transphobia and anti-Semitic memes. "There's been a huge uptick in people trying to vindicate Hitler, and trying to rehabilitate him in the eyes of this young generation," he says. "What they say is things like 'the painter was right'." Faulkner thinks that this neofascism has "petered out a little bit" over the past ten years, but is still on the march. Above all, he sees its resurgence in the genocide of Palestinians in Gaza, and in the qualms many self-described anti-fascists have about condemning it.

It has been revealed that "I and every indigenous person I know, in and out of the games industry, have no nuanced emotions about what is happening there," Faulkner continues. "We know what this is. Like, it's our family stories come to life. We can see what this was. We're not just hearing stories anymore. And we're not just noticing the violence happening to the indigenous people right now. We're noticing how the mostly white, non-indigenous people are still conflicted on it and confused on it, and they don't have clarity on this. The idea with this game was to really bring this into focus, because the games industry likes to say that indigenous people are welcome. And they want to welcome us at our events. What does that mean? You guys want us here to talk, but you're not going to acknowledge the genocide of indigenous people that's happening in front of you, that every single human being at this point knows about.".

According to recent reports, penguin Colony ends with a statement calling out the games industry at large for holding its collective tongue about the Israeli military's brutal campaign, noting that such "cowardice" will be "recorded by the art that it makes". The flipside of that sentiment is that art can be a record of courage and principle, advancing and nourishing a culture in which xenophobia and colonial ideology are unable to thrive. I see this idea expressed, again, in the journey of the Māori group, who are equipped to prevent Psurumin's return because they have made doing so a tradition and a practice.

"They know from generations of story, that you have to do it," says Faulkner. "That it's a responsibility to do it, when it happens." Thwarting Psurumin is part of the Māori's creative lifework, part of their journey together. "It is the job of our descendants to carry forward the story of our resistance," intones one of their group, the game's second narrator. "To create song, dance and story, so our people move toward the light and away from darkness... Every 100 years, to compose latest haka and follow new paths unknown to our enemy.".

According to recent reports, as a whole, Penguin Colony aims to be one such path away from darkness, its methods a mixture of bald and oblique, overt and covert. I have barely broken the surface in this piece. There's an angry hopefulness to the game that coexists with the spectacle of a distinctly 'double-A' penguin bumping and slithering along boulevards of blue-toned, recessed stone. The player is invited to participate in that hope by the game's closing "expedition" screens, which present all the lore you've gathered – including photographs taken by the Nazis, and textual fragments of devious origin – as a web of stars, floating over an illustration of the Zodiac.

According to recent reports, the invocation of constellations is gently subversive because a constellation is an act of selective reading, stringing together sparks in a void. Treat the lore as something you can individually exhaust or "100%", as in many RPGs, and your selective reading will vanish into the mass of motes. Rather than 'completing' the star map in solitude, the game invites players to reach out to each other and compare their constellations – a homage to a "pre-social media" era when the distribution of information was less the province of monolithic digital platforms, and also, a framework for political solidarity. "As we live in a world which continues to push us further apart, we invite you to come together, talk, share, and interpret what you saw," the game suggests.

The call isn't open to all, however. Penguin Colony is consciously designed to repel those who might identify with its Nazis, appropriating the portrayal much as alt-right memesters sought to deify Anakin Skywalker, in the run-up to this year's US midterms. As a rhetorical apparatus, Penguin Colony is full of traps, easily overlooked if you focus on its headline politics. "We have a character voiced by a German trans woman – they can't enjoy it," notes Faulkner. "It just makes their skin crawl." There are many more such snares in the game. The commentary on Israel and Palestine, especially, pervades Penguin Colony in ways I don't think any player has yet discovered.

The lore of Penguin Colony also harbours clues about Origame's future "inherently indigenous" Lovecraftian games. The next game in that trilogy was actually conceived before Penguin Colony, and will be set decades from now. Faulkner envisages it as a loose retelling of Shadows Over Innsmouth, Lovecraft's story about fishpeople cults and miscegenation in a remote coastal town. "It's this idea of, what does Lovecraft look like in a future that we're heading towards, in the sense of social isolation and landscapes of small town decay.".

In a recent development, in place of a Dagon cult, Origame Digital's next game will focus on groups of secretive violent bigots, with the player playing the part of a detective - a premise that, more superficially, makes me eager for a resurrection of the photography mechanics in Origame's reputation-making Umurangi Generation. As with Penguin Colony, the concept draws heavily on Faulkner's own life experiences.

According to recent reports, "I grew up in a cattle town, and cattle towns are notoriously pretty racist places," he indicates. "The whole thing is when I left the town, when I was 18, just because I was going to university, I learned that the town had an active KKK [branch] that was being run out of the Anglican church. And this town is one town away from Grafton, which is where the white supremacist terrorist Brenton Tarrant is from – the guy who went and shot up the mosque in Christchurch. How does that happen? Where everyone knows about it, but they hush up?" The forthcoming game will look at how bitterness and neglect may give rise to such hatred, as local economies dry up and support structures are stripped away.

The second game will also take inspiration from the North American concept of a "sundown town", in which non-white people face violence if they linger outdoors after sunset - a vicious history also explored in Matt Ruff's HBO-adapted novel Lovecraft Country. "I went through a substantial rabbit hole on Youtube of hearing stories of people talking about, like, getting lost on the highway, needing to stop for gas, and then realising they had to stop it for gas at a sundown town," Faulkner explains. "They stopped there. They go to pay. And the clerk just sort of gives them a look, and then nudges over to them that there's a guy in the back of the shop just looking at them. And then suddenly they're followed on the highway for an hour.".

The final game in Origame Digital's planned trilogy is far more formless, right now, but Faulkner has dreams of venturing into the realm of cooperative multiplayer. "It's not even written down on paper yet," he notes. "We've just talked about it. For one thing, I don't know if I've got the skills to do it, because Penguin Colony had some jank, and had some technical complications at launch, but I'm getting better at making games.".

This multiplayer project would build on Penguin Colony's premise of playing a colony, hopping between penguin bodies while shadowing Blakely's expedition. It would also follow through on the former game's closing encouragement to make allies against inhumanity via the collective interpretation of a celestial expanse of lore. "It's about the whole group, and I think if the third one was going to make a point about coming together to solve the problem… you probably want to make that a mechanical issue," Faulkner speculates, "where we have to actually make players do these sorts of actions together.".

📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

Adam Driver has talked more about his unmade Star Wars movie, The Hunt for Ben Solo.

The film was set to pick up after The Rise of Skywalker on the Star Wars timeline with Steven Soderbergh directing, however Disney rejected the project even though it had secured Lucasfilm's approval.

"We were going to do a Ben Solo movie and that didn't happen," Driver told the Talk Easy with Sam Fragoso podcast. "And we worked on it for a long time. Just to highlight, Soderbergh did that for nothing, because we were given a lot of confidence that – Kathy's [Kathleen Kennedy] like, 'We have a 100% approval rate.'.

In a recent development, "And we worked on it. No one's paying us to work on it," he continued. "The only reason why we're working on it was because we fucking loved the idea, how we wanted to do it, and I loved that character. And that was it. That was our guiding principle. All the money stuff came later. And we were trying to figure out how to make it cheap so they could let us do what we wanted to do. So, that was a bummer.".

Recent findings suggest that as for the reason why the film was rejected, Driver mentioned: "Well, the explanation I was told – I'm not going to guess someone else's intention – but the reason that we got was because Ben Solo was dead. That was the response that we got.".

Industry observers note that despite a passionate campaign to resurrect the film, Driver has previously indicated that he thinks it's unlikely it will ever see the light of day. "If they wanted to, fine. But we're not… It's not our call," he has shared. "I think the ship has sailed, though.".

Next up for Star Wars is Ahsoka season 2, which lands on January 20, 2027. In the meantime, check out our guide to all the upcoming Star Wars movies and TV highlights for everything else that's on the way.

  • Recent findings suggest that while the move's been declared this week, Lilja will properly become boss from January 4th, making this a case of getting a new figurehead in place as the calendars swap.

📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

It has been revealed that paradox Interactive, publishers of umpteen strategy genre stalwarts including Crusader Kings, Europa Universalis, and Hearts of Iron, have announced plans to switch overlords early next year. Fredrik Wester will make way for Mattias Lilja, as the deputy CEO takes the throne.

Recent findings suggest that while the move's been declared this week, Lilja will properly become boss from January 4th, making this a case of getting a new figurehead in place as the calendars swap. Departing CEO Fredrik Wester isn't going far, at least for now, as he'll "continue focusing on the manufacturer's long-term development as a member of the board".

"My plan was never to be CEO for life," Wester remarked. "The goal was to build the foundation before passing the baton on for the next chapter in the company’s journey. Since I returned as CEO, we’ve streamlined our strategy, rebuilt our pipeline and developed our commercial offering. Mattias has had a central role in laying this foundation, and now is the right time to hand over.".

Recent findings suggest that "The Board wants to thank Fredrik for his visionary leadership and outstanding contributions over these years," stated chairman Håkan Sjunnesson. "As a result, Paradox is in a strong position at a time when much of the industry is facing major challenges." He added that Lilja is "more than ready to assume the role and lead Paradox towards newly introduced gaming experiences that last for decades".

Lilja himself declared that Paradox have "a unique DNA that has made us one of the greats in deep and engaging strategy and management games" and will be "stepping up the pace". "We will make further investments in our core business, push the boundaries of our game design, work even more closely with our loyal players, develop more and better tools and services that benefit both modders and players, and continue to sharpen our ways of working and our organisation, with player value in focus," he said.

As Wester alluded to, he previously served as Paradox CEO from 2009 to 2018, with a brief stint as executive chairman of the board sandwiched between that and his latest stint as CEO since 2021. Lilja has been deputy CEO since 2024 and chief of staff since 2021, having originally joined Paradox as a producer in 2009.

It has been revealed that the past half decade has been a very mixed bag for Paradox. Their big strategy flagships keep ticking along, albeit with the question of whether their next DLC will feel worth it hovering overhead near-permanently. Outside of that, however, the likes of Cities: Skylines 2, Vampire: The Masquerade Bloodlines 2, and cancelled Sims competitor Life By You have made for a track record heavy on questionable decisions and games which either flopped hard or failed to blow away expectations. Wester acknowledged back in 2024 that the company had "made the wrong calls in several projects, especially outside of our core".

With the likes of post-apocalyptic strategy game Afterworld currently in the works, it'll be interesting to see if Lilja's tenure can see Paradox finally start to nail not just their nerdy bread and butter, but also games that don't involve staring down at a massive map.

📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

Sources indicate that the Sims 4 will soon get a newly introduced revision to resolve a number of issues, some of which have long caused headaches for players. The latest update will arrive March 17 on PC and Mac, followed by PlayStation and Xbox at an unspecified time later.

Outside of the fixes themselves, the patch also makes good on the recent re-commitment to continue improving quality of life for players, so there’s plenty here longtime players will appreciate.

In the latest episode of The Sims 4’s Laundry List blog series, where the developer goes through the most reported problems with the game and how it aims to solve them, we got a rundown of what to expect from next week’s patch.

You can look forward to five major fixes in this one, but arguably the most notable is a change to how Sims determine who they speak with on a lot. This is especially relevant for public lots, where Sims would sometimes interrupt ongoing conversations by barging in and starting a conversation with your Sim.

In a recent development, going forward, Sims will prioritise familiar Sims with whom they already have rapport, and be less likely to latch onto strangers. If you’ve witnessed a date your Sim was on get interrupted because of that, you’ll certainly appreciate the change.

Industry observers note that speaking of budding romance, Prom is coming back to in-game Calendars, and Sims can once again attend. Maxis said this will work with new and existing saves, and that you should also expect Prom goals to be completable once again.

According to recent reports, pets and animals get some love in this patch, too. First, pets and horses will no longer get lost in Premade Households. The fix prevents that from happening in upcoming saves, but if you already had that happen to you in your current save, it’ll still be there.

You may now also assign animals to an Animal Shed after moving your house to a upcoming lot, so you hopefully won’t be confused as to why they’re stuck in your inventory. This fix applies to existing saves as well as new ones.

Lower down the list of urgent fixes is an upgrade that makes it so Sims’ eye blinking will show fully closed eyes for most interactions. The upcoming patch also comes with a host of Sims autonomy fixes, including one that prevents them from excessively flirting with each other.

Catch up on the full list at the link near the top of the page. And, in case you missed it, Maxis recently announced that The Sims 4 will soon get paid mods, something that many in the community are skeptical about.

Industry observers note that that's right, this one is coming to Switch on 14th January 2027. In it, you play as the sovereign of the titular tower, thrust into power after the untimely demise of your predecessor and tasked with keeping the kingdom up and running. To do so, you'll have to recruit knights and match their unique skills to tasks across the land — nabbing stolen manuscripts, taking down evil beings, negotiating with vampires, you know the drill.

There's a rewind function for when things go south, and you can even romance some of those handsome knights you'll meet along the way.

Here's a brief rundown of its key features and a handful of screens so you can soak in the cool visuals:.

According to recent reports, your Reign, Your Rules - Every choice you make defines your legacy and the fate of your kingdom. Recruit eccentric Knights - Manage a court of unpredictable heroes with substantial egos and even bigger problems. Manage Your Round Table - Send knights on epic quests where success or disaster hinges on your judgment. Bend Time and Tempt Fate - Uncover secrets, pursue forbidden romances, and when it all goes wrong, rewind time like they never happened in the first place. Expand Your Tower - Build upcoming annexes, acquire upgrades, and outwit rival rulers in increasingly impressive displays of sovereignty.

January is already filling up with Switch releases, but this could just end up being one to look out for.

📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

It has been revealed that use of generative AI in game dev remains as contentious as it does ubiquitous—a recent GDC report found that around 40% of devs use AI, but more than half think its influence has been negative. Ubisoft is continuing to double down on the technology, this time with Motherbrain, a newly introduced subsidiary fashioned from the team behind its "first playable generative AI experience.".

As reported by VGC, Motherbrain's purpose is to develop "AI for gameplay innovation, supporting all game creators in developing groundbreaking experiences … Its current focus is on upcoming player experiences, smart NPCs with memory and AI game masters that manage large scale systemic worlds," according to an earnings report which was released Thursday.

The information comes at a turbulent time for the publishing giant, which just laid off 166 employees even after Assassin's Creed Black Flag Resynced "outperformed expectations." A sweeping internal overhaul earlier this year saw the manufacturer reorganize its workforce into a throng of "creative houses," a decision which led to swathes of layoffs and six project cancellations, including the Prince of Persia: The Sands of Time Remake.

It's not clear what Motherbrain are at work on, in specific terms, right now, but there may be some clues in its past work. That playable AI "experience" I mentioned earlier is none other than Teammates, an R&D project based on a prior experiment with uncanny AI "neo-NPCs.".

Sources indicate that teammates aimed to allow players to command NPC squadmates in a rudimentary shooter game with a microphone, and using AI, have those squadmates react believably. It's not far off, at least conceptually, from what we've seen in games like Where Winds Meet and Fortnite, both of which have experimented with AI-powered NPCs.

💡 Key Takeaways

📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

It has been revealed that what's the best prank you ever pulled on a teacher in school, assuming you went to school? By which I mean, a genuinely funny prank that didn't cause any injuries, break any of the more key laws (legal or ethical), or leave anybody with years of mental distress.

I'll start: I once had to write a four-page punishment essay with the topic "silence is golden", after being caught talking in class. I took the essay very seriously for the first three pages, only to end it with the phrase "...but not as golden as my arse." The teacher who set me the essay smugly tore it up without reading it - as I knew he would. Checkmate, Mr Thompson. Decades later, the last laugh remains mine.

Worst Class Ever is a new don't-call-it-friendslop asymmetrical multiplayer game dedicated to such larks. One player is a teacher, and seven others are naughty delinquent children, hiding in amongst some well-brought-up and obedient NPCs. As the wayward tykes, your goal is to do mischievous things like eating at your desk, passing notes, dropping banana skins, and playing on your phone, without being spotted by Teach.

Industry observers note that all of this takes place in a breezy modern Japanese high school, the kind familiar from a million animes. Bagsy the Protagonist Desk by the window at the back of the class! The maplist spans the curriculum, from computer labs to gym tracks to stepped lecture theatres. I don't think there are any covert edu-tainment mechanics, but if you're playing Teacher, I guess there's nothing to stop you actually explaining the periodic table while trying to work out who keeps throwing chalk at your head.

What a wholesome and whimsical place! Such happy memories! Oh crikey, the male teacher is terrifying – why can't he stop grinning? And why do I have a smoke grenade? Why is this lesson taking place in the dark? Why are the teachers permitted to punch the students and tie them to wooden posts? Worst Class Ever definitely isn't a horror game, but I'm not sure I'd send my kids to this particular institution. I feel like we're one texture pack away from playing a more sociable version of Little Nightmares. Read more on Steam.

💡 Key Takeaways
  • Crimson Desert is a little over one week away from release, and developer Pearl Abyss has delivered the official, final list of specs for the game.
  • The specs are decently detailed, but more surprisingly - except for a single instance - they don’t include upscaling on PC, another thing games have gotten too comfortable using, even with their lowest specs.
  • Sources indicate that on the official Crimson Desert website, developer Pearl Abyss has delivered a chunky post breaking down five different sets of PC requirements for the upcoming open-world action RPG.
📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

Crimson Desert is a little over one week away from release, and developer Pearl Abyss has delivered the official, final list of specs for the game. The twist is that the specs not only include useful information for PC players, they also cover similarly relevant details for console players, who traditionally don’t get mentioned in those reveals.

The specs are decently detailed, but more surprisingly - except for a single instance - they don’t include upscaling on PC, another thing games have gotten too comfortable using, even with their lowest specs.

Sources indicate that on the official Crimson Desert website, developer Pearl Abyss has delivered a chunky post breaking down five different sets of PC requirements for the upcoming open-world action RPG. Each set indicates the graphics preset being used - and crucially, the resolution and framerate targets you can expect with each.

With the exception of the Minimum spec, all other presets do not appear to rely on upscaling of any kind. They do not say, however, whether ray tracing is being used with any of them, which is a feature that will throw all of those specs out of whack.

It has been revealed that that same transparency also extends to non-PC platforms, which traditionally get few, if any, details about their own resolution and framerate targets. The console set of specs are extensive, just like PC, covering both PlayStation, and Xbox.

It has been revealed that it’s granular enough to indicate which upscaling tech is being used, where applicable. This is relevant for owners of a PS5 Pro, a console that has access to Sony’s PSSR upscaling, alongside the standard AMD FSR tech the base console - and Xbox - use.

The developer has also revealed the base resolution for each mode across each console, and the resolution the image will be upscaled to using whichever tech is being utilised.

And, if you’re one of the five people who play games on Mac, you’ll be thrilled to know that the specs also include a section for Mac devices, split between the different Mac chips. The quality preset being used with each is not clear, however.

Finally, there's a set of specs for the Rog Xbox Ally, covering both the X and S models.

Recent findings suggest that crimson Desert arrives March 20 on PC, PS5, and Xbox Series X/S. You can expect more coverage from us at release and beyond.

While soulslikes went bigger than significant, Death's Door swung open the appeal of a tighter adventure

📅 13 Nov 2026 | ⏱️ 3 min read (555 words, 📚 Deep Dive) | Source: Rockpapershotgun

⏱️ ~3 mins left to finish
📖 0% read
💡 Key Takeaways
  • Declaring a Best Way of Doing Things is a fool’s game, though in recent years my favourite entries in the Tricky Hitting genre – inclusive of soulslikes and their hybridised disciples – have been the major, bulging ones.
  • Sources indicate that even in the latter stages, with a full kit of precisely four ranged spells, Death’s Door is a simple proposition.
  • Still, it’s clever with its limitations.
📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

Declaring a Best Way of Doing Things is a fool’s game, though in recent years my favourite entries in the Tricky Hitting genre – inclusive of soulslikes and their hybridised disciples – have been the major, bulging ones. Elden Rings and Silksongs, with vast kingdoms and deep, rattling toolkits for surviving them. The reason it’s a fool’s game is because you can also have something like Death’s Door, a taut, compact, lighthearted little actioner that fills eight hours instead of 80 and yet never feels underwhelming or compromised for it.

Sources indicate that even in the latter stages, with a full kit of precisely four ranged spells, Death’s Door is a simple proposition. You are a crow. You hit things. Occasionally you shoot things. You collect the souls of a frog, a yeti, and a grandmother. Everything in-between directly relates to finding the errant monster/pensioner, or at a stretch, upgrading one of those four abilities.

Still, it’s clever with its limitations. Environments are small in number but vary wildly in tone and texture, and they tightly weave their paths into criss-crossing bundles that maximise travel – evoking the sense of a great, ranging adventure within relatively tiny spaces. The lack of a wiki’s worth of combat options also never becomes a problem, partly because it spreads out its spell unlocks, and partly because the smooth, flowing back-and-forths of its central swordplay are pleasurable enough to carry it anyway. Good bosses, too! They’re all characterful, memorable weirdoes who fight unlike anyone in their minion armies, and usually come with a hidden weakness to deduce and exploit.

Which is welcome, as these big lads and lasses do tend to launch difficulty spikes right up your feathered backside, and do so in a game that isn’t otherwise as fussed about trial-and-error pain endurance as some of its inspirations. They don’t, however, bring the mood down. At times, this tale of a pitch-black soul reaper working as an agent of Death (complete with an office of Death and embittered co-workers of Death) can get downright cosy, leading through you through warmly-lit jungles and breezy waterside ruins.

Recently replaying, I’d also forgotten how witty it can be. Little gaglets are sprinkled throughout, both visual and verbal, but the best jokes are saved for – funnily enough – the bosses, who’ll raise your pre-fight spirit with some amusingly terrible trash talk before becoming the punchline themselves. I audibly wheezed the first time a death animation immediately cut to the foe’s impromptu funeral, their beaked killer among the precious few guests. And even when the joke is recycled later, I couldn’t help tittering at the sight of my enemy – who seconds earlier, had been attempting to fatally sit on me – lying nobly in state.

According to recent reports, I previously considered ending my Valor Mortis review by calling it a gateway into the more demanding side of action-RPGs; a shorter, simpler alternative to FromSoft’s overwhelming titans that might nonetheless serve to introduce curious newcomers to their shared quirks and qualities. The game equivalent of splashing your chest with water before jumping into a pool. In hindsight, Death’s Door was always a better fit for that description, though there’s enough else here you don’t need to be prepping for something tougher to appreciate its lean, keen adventuring.

Battlefield 6 is getting a free trial next week with a decent selection of maps and modes

📅 13 Mar 2026 | ⏱️ 3 min read (556 words, 📚 Deep Dive) | Source: Vg247

📖 0% read
💡 Key Takeaways
  • In a recent development, battlefield Studios has revealed that Battlefield 6 is going free to play for one week next week.
  • Recent findings suggest that though it does not encompass the entirety of the game, the free trial is fairly generous.
  • For starters, the trial kicks off Tuesday, March 17 and will run until the following Tuesday, March 24.
📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

In a recent development, battlefield Studios has revealed that Battlefield 6 is going free to play for one week next week. Well, a portion of the game is, anyway, as part of a free trial that will include some of the game’s most popular modes and maps.

Recent findings suggest that though it does not encompass the entirety of the game, the free trial is fairly generous. Here’s what to expect.

For starters, the trial kicks off Tuesday, March 17 and will run until the following Tuesday, March 24. The trial will be accessible from Battlefield Redsec, the already free-to-play portion of the game.

Once downloaded, you’ll find a newly introduced Battlefield 6 Free Trial section in the main menu. Because Redsec and Battlefield 6 multiplayer share progression, if you played the former at any point, you’ll be able to pick up from where you left off.

The same is also true the other way around; if this is your first time with Battlefield 6, all your unlocks will carry over to the full version, as well as to Redsec if you decide stick with the free-to-play off-shoot.

Industry observers note that once it kicks off, you’ll find three playlists to choose from. Casual Breakthrough, All-out Warfare, and a third playlist showcasing the new Nightfall game mode and its associated map.

According to recent reports, all-out Warfare is what you come to Battlefield for, and that playlist features Conquest, Breakthrough, as well as BF6’s newcomer Escalation - all large-scale, combined arms game modes. They will be playable across four maps. You get to play on two from Season 2: Contaminated, and Hagental Base, one from Season 1: Eastwood, and Mirak Valley from the base game.

According to recent reports, casual Breakthrough is based on a playlist that already exists in the core game, and it’s really designed as a nice on-ramp for new players. It also offers less intense gameplay, perfect for people grinding unlocks.

Casual Breakthrough is limited to just 16 real players (eight per team), with the rest filled up with bots. You earn the same amount of XP in those matches, except when you interact with bots, so killing a bot will net less than a human player. Outside of that, unlocks, Challenges and all other things that don’t depend on stat-tracking can be done within.

In the trial, the Casual Breakthrough playlist includes Hagental Base, Contaminated, and Eastwood.

The most interesting is the third playlist, in part because its content will also be available to owners of the full game for the first time right alongside free-to-play players. Nightfall is a playlist exclusive to the Hagental Base map.

In a recent development, this is a very small map, so the mode selection here is Team Deathmatch, Squad Deathmatch, and Domination. Under Nightfall conditions, lights across the entire map are turned off, so you’re going to have use your NVGs to be able to see. This is also a god opportunity to try out weapon attachments that specifically work under low-light conditions, which typically don’t get much use in multiplayer.

March 17 also marks the launch of the second stage of Battlefield 6’s Season 2, which comes with the aforementioned Nightfall content, as well as a massive newly introduced update - so the timing works out nicely for everyone.

📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

The good (and hilarious) folks over at HDTVTest have been looking at the HDR Calibration settings for GTA 6 on PS5 and Xbox Series X|S, and they've discovered that the tool is actually slightly broken as things stand.

Some of the specifics go over my head a little bit to be honest, but in a nutshell, the figures that are displayed on the calibration tool don't fully translate into the game itself, leading to a potentially inoptimal picture.

As a result, they've published a fresh nine-minute video (which you can see up above) to explain the issues.

"The HDR calibration screen in GTA 6 can be misleading, because Rockstar's Max Brightness, Paper White and Black Levels settings interact in unexpected ways. To be clear, GTA VI's HDR rendering isn't broken… it's the calibration procedure that can give misleading results.".

The video goes step-by-step on how they analysed the complications and tried to figure out the best possible HDR settings for GTA 6, and while their tests aren't fully concluded yet (there's another video to come in the future where they try multiple consumer displays), they've shared their initial best settings for displays capable of 1,000 nits or brighter.

Here are those three settings, but again, keep in mind that your TV must be capable of 1,000 nits of brightness or more, and that certain smart TV features or special HDR settings on your TV itself may interfere with the results.

If your display isn't capable of 1,000 nits, do a bit of Googling to try and find out the specifics for your TV/monitor, and then times that figure by two in-game. So, if you're working with a maximum of 600 nits, set the figure as 1,200.

I have to be honest and say I'm not seeing a lot of difference here, but I've also got an old TV with a max brightness of just over 600 nits, not to mention I'm using a few image-altering features that may be playing havoc with the settings. It's also noted in the video that this is generally based on playing in the dark, rather than in a brightly-lit room.

Have a play for yourself and see what you think - there's clearly a lot of people who are very thankful for these settings on YouTube and beyond, so we wanted to at least make you aware of them. The reality is that you may need to still do a bit of tweaking to find the perfect sweet spot for your setup though.

💡 Key Takeaways

📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

GTA 6 got off to a record-breaking start with its day-one sales, bringing in $3.79 billion by launch day thanks to 32.5 million pre-orders, but one analyst estimates its launch weekend numbers are on par with Spider-Man: Brand Latest Day and The Odyssey combined – and even eclipsed Taylor Swift's Eras tour. Sorry, Swifties.

Rhys Elliott of Alinea Analytics reckons that by the end of the weekend, GTA 6 had sold through a whopping 44.9 million copies across PS5 and Xbox Series X|S. Matching previous estimates from Sensor Tower, he believes that around three-quarters of those sales were on PS5 (accounting for roughly 33.7 million copies, with 11.2 million on Xbox).

To put it into perspective, the analyst says this accounts for "around 30% of the installed base per platform," so almost a third of owners of each console have bought the game.

This would place GTA 6's revenue at $4 billion in four days, Elliott notes, noting that it's "roughly equal to the year’s two summer blockbusters combined (Spider-Man and The Odyssey)." Per data from Box Office Mojo, Spider-Man: Brand Latest Day earned over $2.5 billion from its worldwide box office revenue, while The Odyssey brought in over $1.8 billion. Combined, they're at just over $4.3 billion, so this comparison tracks – and it clearly won't take Rockstar Games long to overtake them, either, given what it's achieved in just four days.

"GTA 6 has also made twice as much as Taylor Swift's entire Eras Tour grossed across its whole run," Elliott adds. The Guardian reported in late 2024 that as of the final show of the Eras Tour, ticket revenue was at around $2.08 billion, not counting merch sales. "GTA 6 did that between Thursday and Sunday, and that's before the PC port and GTA Online," he adds.

Alinea Analytics' daily active user (DAU) estimates are also extremely strong, as you'd expect. "Our DAU estimates show that around 40.8M people logged in to play GTA 6 yesterday (Sunday Nov 22), about 76% on PS5," Elliott notes. "And roughly 20% of players – almost 9M folks – have racked up over 20 hours in Leonida.".

It has been revealed that there was never any doubt that GTA 6 was going to be huge, but this really is something else. With the many, many 10/10 GTA 6 reviews, too, things really couldn't be going much better for Rockstar right now.

📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

A newly introduced Honkai: Star Rail Special Program has concluded, which means some fresh news about the game’s upcoming major update. Version 4.1, unveiled today as Unraveled for Daybreak, is the action RPG’s next moment, kicking off on March 25.

Unraveled for Daybreak is the next chapter in the ongoing story of Planarcadia, with the Astra Express Crew now invited to a fan fest inspired by their own past journeys. The aptly named Star Rail Fest is ostensibly hosted to allow more of the citizens of Arcadia to experience the Trailblaze.

Recent findings suggest that as everyone’s eyes is fixated on the grand Star Rail Fest, the Phantasmoon Games continue to be in full swing, as does the war with the Supplicants. Star Rail Fest is, however, the major focus of this upgrade, in case it wasn't obvious.

Sources indicate that the event is made up of three large-scale zones, each themed around past excursions of the Astral Express. You’ll get to explore the Belobog Zone, Xianzhou Luofu Zone, and Penacony Zone. Later on, you’ll also be able to visit Pearluxe Tower, the headquarters of Pearluxe Corp.

Each area will feature its own attractions, such as the balloon figures of Supreme Guardian Cocolia and the Destruction Engine, the duel against the Lord Ravager Phantylia at Scalegorge Waterscape, and the Pearluxe Tower’s Alloy King Pom-Pom model.

It has been revealed that the hot new arrival is bumbling noirish detective Ashveil whom we've met in Version 4.0, and who becomes a playable character with this patch. Ashveil is a 5-Star Lightning-Type character, on the Path of The Hunt. You’ll be able to pull for him throughout 4.1's runtime, which is slightly reduced at four weeks instead of the usual six, in order to rebalance the schedule after the extra-long Version 3.8.

In a recent development, in combat, Ashveil is capable of increasing Crit Damage of all allies. He can also mark an enemy as Bait, which reduces the Defence of all enemies on the field so long as this tag holds. If Ashveil uses his Skill on the baited target, he will deal extra Damage and regain Skill Points for the team.

It has been revealed that ashveil can bully that baited target even further by launching Hounding Pursuit. If any of his teammates attacks the Bait, he can further deliver a follow-up attack that gradually accumulates Gluttony for as long as he’s in combat. Gluttony can later be consumed to boost follow-up attack damage.

If he lands a kill, Ashveil continues to deal damage to the next enemy he attacks. That buff is transferred if that enemy is killed. Even in map exploration, Ashveil can be deadly, capable of inflicting Stunned upon enemies within a specific range.

Recent findings suggest that returning characters this patch will be Hyacine in the first half, and Boothill in the second half. Once again, due to the reduced runtime, their banner reruns will be slightly shorter than normal, at just two weeks each instead of three — so be sure to take that into account if you're planning on pulling for either of them.

Version 4.1 also adds the Wispae War Saga, a fresh activity where you can practice your leadership skills by commanding different types of Wispae Soldiers in the Graphia Academy. You can upgrade each one, use spell cards to alter their effects, and later face other champions. You ultimately want to play this to unlock new Wispae Companions, not to mention complete the challenges within.

📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

In a recent development, mucky and disreputable kiosk game Probably Stolen – Cyberpunk Shopkeeper Sim is getting three massive updates over the next few months that add extra starting scenarios, building on the existing wealth of goods, materials, vocations and techs. Those starting scenarios range from peddling human meat to running the finest cyber-frappucino stall this side of Tannhäuser Gate. There are no hard release dates, and the contents of each enhancement may alter, but developers Questing Goose Studio have shared some rough timeframes.

Recent findings suggest that coming up in mid-December, there's the Junker starting scenario, which I assume is all about trading scrap, rather than being a Prussian nobleman. You'll get a bespoke perk, newly introduced items, and the ability to hire, equip and send scavs on expeditions. This revision will also include some minor expansions for the Fence and Gunsmith vocations – the latter will be able to flog or otherwise make use of shotgun shells, 25mm grenade rounds and a tier 3 handmade SMG, alongside new armour.

In a recent development, late January is when you'll "very likely" get the chance to be an Organ Dealer, care of the second major revision. "Players will start by buying different organs and fulfilling specific requests, and will later be able to grow or print organs," a Steam blog explains. You'll also be able to filter blood and remove diseases, with different blood types having different value modifiers. How will you get your hands on organs? By sending horrible black market thugs on foraging "expeditions".

Last but not least, the planned April update will add the Street Food Vendor starting scenario. This lets you weave a livelihood around choice beverages and edibles from a range of cultures, supported by updates to the game's Aquaculture and Hydroponics tech. Sounds a lot cheerier than the organ trading racket, but then again, Probably Stolen will doubtless find a way to make it utterly grim. Guests at Sweeney's Cantina know better than to ask what our frappucinos are made of.

According to recent reports, are you playing Probably Stolen? It's been doing better than expected. I was keen on the demo, but my attention was lured away by a truly upsetting game about dogpeople in caves.

📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

Revision [Mon 23rd Nov 2026, 2:20pm]: Nvidia has posted an update confirming that Jensen Huang has now been reinstated as president, CEO, and board member following his earlier resignation.

Sources indicate that the post confirms that Nvidia's board "received input from senior levels of the United States government, and based on that input, the Board is confident that Mr. Huang’s reinstatement poses no national security risk".

Huang resigned following multiple instances of alleged infidelity, most notably with an alleged Chinese spy, leading to concerns over national security as the US and China butt heads in the race to become the dominant force in the world of AI.

Huang also contributed the following message.

According to recent reports, “I am honored to return to NVIDIA and lead one of the most consequential technology companies in the world at the beginning of a latest industrial revolution. I take this responsibility with the greatest humility and renewed commitment. I want to thank the NVIDIA Board for its confidence and deliberation through this process. I am especially grateful to Harvey Jones for his leadership as Chair, and to Colette Kress and our executive staff for leading NVIDIA during this period.

"I am also deeply thankful to our employees, shareholders, leaders across the industry and partners around the world for their extraordinary support. Above all, I am grateful for the love and support of my family. I can’t wait to get back to work.”.

We can only assume that the investigation into Huang's relationships turned up nothing unusual – surely they wouldn't just sweep it under the rug, right?

Meanwhile, US president Donald Trump celebrated Huang's reinstatement, calling him a "Great Patriot and National Treasure" while stating that the decision is vital to "ensure the Success and Prosperity of not only the Tech giant, but the American Economy".

Original Story: Nvidia, one of the largest tech firms in the world and the company responsible for the Switch 2's custom processor, has found itself embroiled in scandal over recent days.

As reported by The Guardian, Nvidia's CEO Jensen Huang, who you might recognise from the 'Creator's Voice Special Edition' video for Switch 2, has now resigned after reported affairs with an alleged Chinese spy and a firm employee.

He will be replaced on an interim basis by Nvidia’s chief financial officer, Colette Kress, until a full-time successor is named. Nvidia's share price began to sharply decline following reports of the scandal, to the point where it is now no longer the most valuable organization in the world.

The BBC speculates that Huang's departure could set him up to be a "formidable opponent" to the very manufacturer he co-founded, with Elon Musk stating that it would be "an honour" to work with him at SpaceX.

In a recent development, with regards to Nintendo, it's likely that none of this will have any immediate impact on Nvidia's relationship with the Japanese company. Nvidia will no doubt be under contract to supply custom chips for the Switch 2, but what happens with the inevitable Switch 2 successor is under question.

Hopefully everything will go smoothly for Nintendo, but if it wants to utilise Nvidia's architecture for its next console – particularly for backwards compatibility – then its efforts may be impacted by Huang's departure along with Nvidia's sharp pivot towards AI.

Of course, it's really early to be speculating about the 'Switch 3', but you can bet that Nintendo's R&D department will be looking at all of this very closely and considering its potential impact.

What are your thoughts on all of this? Could Huang's departure have any effect on Nvidia's business with Nintendo? Let us know with a comment.

📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

While GTA 6 has been receiving unbelievable praise and is technically considered one of the best video games of all time according to Metacritic, that certainly doesn't mean it's immune to criticism.

One of the big talking points both before and after launch has been that it's a 30FPS experience across all Xbox and PlayStation consoles, and if you're going from 60FPS back to 30FPS, there's definitely an adjustment period. Some people are absolutely fine with that, while others are finding it extremely difficult to go back.

For what it's worth, our friends at Digital Foundry have been analysing this in depth today:.

Rockstar Games has already confirmed recently that even the PS5 Pro doesn't come close to running GTA 6 at 60FPS due to the system's processor not being powerful enough, so we might be forced to wait until the next generation of consoles (and PC) before the game will become playable at 60 frames per-second.

"The PS5 Pro features an upgraded graphics processor and upscaling technology that we leverage to increase the game’s visual fidelity. While the PS5 Pro’s central processor is slightly better than the PS5 base console, it is not powerful enough to run the game’s complex simulation at higher frame rates.”.

With all of this in mind, we're interested to hear what you think about playing games at 30FPS on Xbox, PlayStation or anywhere else. It's becoming much more common that 60FPS is the default these days, but there are still some phenomenal 30FPS-only experiences out there, and it's a shame to think people are missing out on them.

I personally much prefer playing at 60FPS if I can, and there are certain games I will avoid at 30FPS until they get a patch down the line (like Mafia: Definitive Edition), but when it comes to industry-defining masterpieces like Red Dead Redemption 2 and Grand Theft Auto VI, the last thing I'd want is for them to scale back the detail in order to squeeze in a 60FPS mode.

Industry observers note that so, what do you think? Tell us in the poll above and in the comments section below.

📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

HoYoverse has delivered another Special Program for the second day running, this time for Zenless Zone Zero. The developer revealed the full details of Version 2.7, subtitled Champions Never Fall to the Past.

This next major revision arrives March 24, adding two new Agents, and introducing the Hollow Champion competition.

Most things in Version 2.7 follow on from the Hollow Champion competition, which brings together old friends and familiar faces, as well interesting newcomers. Everyone is in it to win some big rewards and earn glory.

Recent findings suggest that among the unexpected participants the competition has attracted are the Public Security's Metropolitan Order Division, and even some former Calydon's Sweepers. A big challenge that awaits is Black Wolf Romeul, who’s capable of increasing his Crit Damage Resistance and Interruption Resistance by activating a Corruptive Barrier.

Romeul can also cause enemies to continuously lose HP, but you can beat him by putting together a squad that can deal sustained Anomaly damage, which will break through the barrier promptly.

Our first upcoming arrival in Version 2.7 is Cissia of the Metropolitan Order Division. She is an S-Rank Electric Attack Agent who automatically gains three stacks of Venom when she enters the battle. Each stack deals Electric Damage while also increasing her Crit Rate for a time.

Industry observers note that when she runs out of Venom, which will happen, Cissia can generate more stacks by using her EX Special Attack. She can also use her Basic Attack, Serpent's Kiss, to better utilise the upcoming stacks of Venom she generates.

In a recent development, the other new Agent may be the more exciting. Nangong Yu, the captain and lead dancer of the Angels of Delusion, can now be part of your team. Nangong Yu is an S-Rank Ether Stun Agent who can boost her team’s Anomaly Buildup Rate against Stunned enemies.

Being part of an idol group has its perks, because she automatically regenerates Downbeat as time goes on, and even more any time a squad member inflicts an enemy with Anomaly. Nangong Yu can then use Downbeat - after enough has been accumulated - on charged attacks that keep enemies stunned for longer. Her Ultimate triggers Ether Veil: Delusion Reprise, which boosts the entire squad’s Attack.

Returning Agents in Version 2.7 will be Yidhari, the S-Rank Ice Rupture Agent, as well as Seed, the Electric Attack Agent.

Outside of all the very vital action in the core story, this chapter also brings newly introduced themed events to Lumina Square’s Simmer Hot Pot Restaurant. The Simulated Battle Trial is also getting some love, with updated mechanics and new enemy line-ups.

Catch up on our recently updated Zenless Zone Zero character tier list, and don’t forget to check out these Zenless Zone Zero codes before you jump in for some free stuff.

A massive part of the point of The Blood of Dawnwalker is that you're on a fixed time limit. You've got 30 in-game days and nights to try and save your family, and if you don't manage to see everything the game has to offer, well, the game's director is fine with that. But that doesn't matter as much now, as The Blood of Dawnwalker is getting its 1.2 update next week that adds in a latest game plus mode.

Industry observers note that "If you completed the Epilogue, you can dive right back into Vale Sangora with New Game+!" a post from the devs explains. "Your level, skills, and inventory will carry over; the level cap will be raised to 100; enemies will be balanced and scale uniformly across all regions; and items will have NG+ versions with updated stats." Sounds like your usual new game plus affair! I suppose it is a good opportunity to try out different things compared to your first playthrough, but I'm not exactly aligned with the idea that the timer restriction is too restricting (as some mods have made clear how others feel that way).

In any case, the update goes a tad further than that. If you got the Eclipse Edition of the game, the in-game soundtrack that came with it "will be extended with additional songs from the game." You can expect the soundtrack on streaming services soon, too. While details are slimmer here, there are also some planned balance changes, like updated enemy health pools and how often they use their abilities during combat, and terrain geometry has seen some improvements to allow for "smoother movement during combat and exploration.".

In a recent development, overall, a bit of a smaller patch compared to the last one, but one I'm sure will be welcome to some all the same. If you've not had a chance to check the game out yet and still feel on the fence about it, here's some lovely words from Mark's review: "There’s always that sense that something important or unexpected could be lurking around the next corner, to pull you into a quest dripping with depth and intrigue. It works to ensure the more busywork-esque tasks attached to angering Brencis and his Boyars never make Vale Sangora feel home to a string of boring boxes to tick. It’s a vibrant, constantly changing place with a thousand different threads metaphorically criss-crossing just beneath its surface, just as ancient ruins literally criss-cross beneath its swamps, crags, and forests.".

GTA 6 Is Blowing Away Gaming's Greatest Devs, Including Naughty Dog

⏱️ ~2 mins left to finish
📖 0% read
💡 Key Takeaways
  • Naughty Dog’s Michael Barclay – whose credits include Uncharted: The Lost Legacy and The Last of Us 2 – indicates he’s “made video games for 19 years and GTA 6 appears to me as a Bugatti Veyron would to a nervous Victorian child”.
  • Rockstar’s latest open world release is by far the best-looking game ever made, even if it is locked to 30fps on PS5 hardware.
  • And it’s being treated like witchcraft by devs, who naturally have a greater appreciation for the feats on display.
📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

Naughty Dog’s Michael Barclay – whose credits include Uncharted: The Lost Legacy and The Last of Us 2 – indicates he’s “made video games for 19 years and GTA 6 appears to me as a Bugatti Veyron would to a nervous Victorian child”.

Rockstar’s latest open world release is by far the best-looking game ever made, even if it is locked to 30fps on PS5 hardware.

And it’s being treated like witchcraft by devs, who naturally have a greater appreciation for the feats on display.

Barclay, who’s at the moment working on next year’s Intergalactic: The Heretic Prophet, continued:.

“I'm always astonished that [Rockstar’s] environmental lighting is mostly dynamic and looks as good if not better than most baked lighting.”.

In really, really simple terms, baked lighting is a game development technique used to save computational cost by calculating light and shadow data in advance.

The downside to this is that it’s fixed, but obviously given the ever-changing nature of GTA 6’s sandbox, it needs to have a dynamic solution.

Barclay is saying that GTA 6’s dynamic lighting matches and even surpasses those pre-determined solutions in many scenarios, making it a real accomplishment.

These comments triggered discussion from various other industry professionals, including Tim Soret from Odd Tales, the makers of The Last Night, who outlined some of his thoughts on the title:.

GTA 6 sets a standard so unfathomably high I do wonder at what point it’ll ever be topped.

I suppose raising the bar like this will motivate the many other talented devs around the world, but not every studio will have access to the time and the estimated $1 billion budget that allowed Rockstar to deliver this.

Either way, it’s clear industry professionals are utterly blown away by what the studio has delivered here.

Clearly, though, sometimes you just need to play the hits, as a new release of the original game is on the way in the form of Super Meat Boy Again+, a remaster with updated graphics, levels and plenty more.

📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

Crimson Desert, the open-world action RPG off-shoot from Korean MMO Black Desert Online, has officially rolled out, nearly six years after it was initially revealed. The game has been building up a lot of momentum over the years, which recently coalesced to turn it into one of 2026’s most anticipated titles.

All of it has been leading up to this moment, and the game appears to have landed smoothly, though not without controversy, as has seemingly become part of its MO.

Industry observers note that it has not been 24 hours since Crimson Desert launched on PC and consoles, and it’s already become a massive hit. On Steam, one of two stores where the game can be purchased (the other being the Epic Games Store), the game shot to the top of the charts.

In a recent development, the action RPG continued to accumulate more and more players on Steam, peaking at a very respectable 239,045 concurrent players (via SteamDB). Though its success was very much expected, we perhaps didn’t predict its peak would be that high.

Indeed, Crimson Desert has been in Steam’s top 100 global sellers list for six weeks, jumping up six spots to become the number one seller this week just before it launched. As we get closer to the weekend, the numbers could climb even higher.

This peak concurrent puts Crimson Desert in the same league as several of the other major releases of the first quarter of 2026. The top spot continues to belong to Slay the Spire 2, which peaked at a staggering 574,638 concurrent players. It happened just days after the juggernaut Resident Evil Requiem achieved its own 344,214 peak concurrent, which was the year’s highest up until Slay the Spire 2’s release. All three are well ahead of Nioh 3’s 88,045 peak concurrent, and Marathon’s nearly identical peak of 88,337.

Recent findings suggest that crimson Desert has seen something of a mixed reception by critics. James gave it three stars in our review, saying it “lacks the connective sinew to be truly functional,” which is a common criticism shared by other outlets. Many also lamented the sheer number of systems fighting for player attention, its poorly explained mechanics, and counterintuitive controls.

In a recent development, on Steam, at least, players have similarly been divided, with the current Steam user rating sitting at Mixed, based on 8,728 reviews. Unsurprisingly, most of the negative reactions fall on the clunky controls and the game’s tendency to, as one Steam user put it, “so miserably tries to be everything at once, and fails to be anything at all.”.

In a recent development, if you’re just getting started in Crimson Desert yourself, or initiative to do so soon, we recommend reading these crucial tips to help orient yourself in the game’s vast world. You should also plan your initial skill unlocks by prioritising these skills to spend your Abyss Artifacts first.

It's hard to know if you're getting a good price for a booster or bundle. That's even the case during the Black Friday sales; is a discount actually offering you a solid reduction, or is it just offering a tiny reduction from the inflated price?

That's a question I set off to solve in Walmart's Black Friday Pokémon TCG sales. The retailer has loads of pack discounts, but to varying degrees. So I looked through each one, and compared the discounted price to its actual market price, using several websites which chart this cost. Each of the 10 boosters and bundles you'll find below is now nearly at, on, or even cheaper than, its 'standard' price; these are real deals, and you can feel secure that you're actually getting a discount. They're certainly some of the better Black Friday Pokemon card deals, anyway.

According to recent reports, this sextet of Scarlet & Violet booster packs is back down to its market price thanks to the $15 discount. That's 60 cards, for about $1 each.

Walmart has this Chaos Rising blister, featuring three boosters and a Charmeleon card, for slightly less than most other retailers thanks to this 43% discount. It also offers one of the best price-per-card deals of this list.

For some reason, Walmart has multiple listings for this Elite Trainer Box, with each sitting at a different price. This $116 bundle is the cheapest, and it matches the general market price for this set. It includes various packs including boosters, foil energy cards, sleeves, damage-counter dice and a fancy collectors'' box.

While $10 may not seem like a massive saving, again it's bringing this bundle of 6 Pitch Black booster packs to its market price. That's 6 packs for $40, undercutting some other similar packs from other series.

It has been revealed that another Mega Evolution six-booster bundle, but with a twist: this is about $7 cheaper than the average market price for the bundle. That makes it one of the best deals of the list, in terms of beating other costs.

This massive bundle usually goes for about $118, so you're getting it at pre-inflated prices right now. The Trainer Box isn't just for booster packs, but it has energy cards, sleeves, die, condition markers and more.

The market price for this set is $124, so you're getting it at a reasonable price, although some other Trainer Boxes on this list are cheaper.

According to recent reports, this 6-booster bundle from Destined Rivals isn't technically at market price, but only by about $2, so it's close enough to be a worthy discount. It's one of the pricier booster bundles on this list, but that still means it's much cheaper than non-discounted ones!

While this wouldn't seem like a huge saving, at 17% off, it brings the Trainer Box down to only $1 off its standard market price. If the previous Chaos Rising bundle isn't massive enough for you, this is a much larger alternative.

We're looking at a discounted price that's about $6 higher than the best market price you're getting for the Trainer Box. Like others of its kind, you don't just get cards but dice and counters.

If you've been clicking through on some of these Pokémon TCG deals, you'll have noticed that some are low in stock. If there's a bundle or Trainer Box you're particularly interested in, it might be worth jumping on the discount before it sells out.

When Black Friday properly begins around November 27, we'll likely see other retailers pick up steam in the Pokémon TCG deals department — when I price checked these picks, I didn't see a huge amount of competition, but I expect that'll change soon.

According to recent reports, however with how vast the TCG ecosystem is, there's no telling whether it'll be these exact same sets that'll see discounts. If you're just looking for a few boosters, you're probably fine waiting, but the more advanced sets may not get any discounts from other retailers. That's all to say that if these are sets you want, it's probably worth buying them. But if you had your heart set on another pack, it may be worth waiting, rather than settling for something you see here that's similar.
